Title: What our people are doing with AI
Owner: Cyber AI adoption lead + champions from all six functions
Why internal: N1 needs credible examples from colleagues, evidence of results and a clear distinction between available tools and emerging capabilities.
Agenda: 10m orientation; 35m two colleague-led case demonstrations including a failure and its correction; 15m an emerging or restricted-pilot demonstration; 15m domain application; 15m knowledge check and reflection. Use a short case gallery to represent all six functions without six separate lectures.
Assessment evidence: N1.1: explain one own-domain and one neighbouring-domain use case, including limitations. N1.2: distinguish production, restricted pilot and horizon examples. N1.3: propose two or three changes to own work and identify retained human accountability.
Prerequisites: Case owners provide verified examples, permission to demonstrate them, evidence of results and current tool-access status.

Title: Our approved tools, agent architecture and boundaries
Owner: AI platform owner + IAM + IDP + security architecture
Why internal: Only internal owners can establish the approved platforms, data routes, identities, access limits and escalation mechanisms.
Agenda: 25m model, modality and agent walkthrough; 25m approved platforms, data flow and connector permissions; 20m approval, logs and stop controls; 20m access/data-boundary decisions. Use one real approved architecture with a simplified diagram.
Assessment evidence: Label model, harness, tools and controls; select the permitted platform for a data class; distinguish available access from a pilot; locate the correct approval, stop and escalation route.
Prerequisites: Current platform inventory, data-handling rules, approved access routes, accessible demonstration and reviewed diagrams.

Title: Safe use in my job — coached case and Gate 1
Why internal: A local exercise tests judgement against the bank rules after the external foundation, without repeating general AI-awareness content.
Agenda: 15m coached case; 30m individual safe-use scenario; 15m feedback. Use approved or synthetic data and a task representative of the learner’s function.
Assessment evidence: Reject an unsafe data/tool choice, detect a planted unsupported claim or injection, verify the output and record accountability. Safety-critical decisions must pass.
Prerequisites: Independent answer key, domain case variants, accessible format and calibrated assessor checklist.

Title: Supervise and recover an agent on our platform
Owner: Domain operations owner + AI platform team
Why internal: Supervision depends on the actual console, action permissions, logs, approvals and recovery runbook.
Agenda: 30m workflow and permissions; 60m trace-review and planted-error lab; 30m stop, revoke, rollback and manual-fallback exercise.
Assessment evidence: Delegate within an approved action class, inspect permissions and changes, identify planted failures, stop/revoke safely and produce an accountable handover.
Prerequisites: Stable approved sandbox or realistic simulation, seeded traces and a tested recovery path.

Title: Create, own and retire a shared Skill
Owner: Domain automation champion + Skill-library owner + IAM
Why internal: The catalogue has no evidenced teaching for Skill maintenance and shared-library ownership; internal conventions must be taught directly.
Agenda: 30m worked example and third-party vetting; 60m create a focused Skill and safe connector specification; 30m peer review, ownership, monthly review and deprecation.
Assessment evidence: Submit a trigger, steps, expected output, failure modes and tests; name an owner and review/deprecation rule; justify connector permissions and provenance.
Prerequisites: Agreed Skill template, library workflow, ownership rules, approved connector list and model-change notification route.

Title: Domain test cases and release checks
Why internal: Useful benchmark answers and known faults come from the function’s own work; a generic course cannot supply the approved cases.
Agenda: 30m independent answers and known faults; 60m build and run five representative cases with pass/fail checks; 30m simulate a model/Skill change and submit results to the domain evaluation process.
Assessment evidence: Versioned cases, known faults and acceptance checks; rerun record; contribution to the shared domain evidence store.
Prerequisites: Labelled cases, approved data, a simple supported evaluation harness and result-submission format.

Title: Agent-supervisor observed sign-off
Why internal: Course completion cannot establish safe operational supervision in this environment.
Agenda: 75m observed task with injected faults and a connector change; 30m independent challenge; 15m feedback and scope-of-authority record.
Assessment evidence: Pass each safety-critical action and justify an evidence-based release decision. Record permitted action classes and any remediation.
Prerequisites: Assessor calibration and test cases withheld from coached practice.

Title: Workflow and supervision design studio
Owner: Process owner + technical lead + operational supervisor
Why internal: N14 concerns real workflow allocation, approval gates, workload and accountability. A workshop with the actual process owner is more actionable than generic organisational-redesign teaching.
Agenda: 45m map current work; 60m redesign tasks and approval points; 45m review evaluation evidence and supervision load; 30m agree measures and ownership.
Assessment evidence: An approved before/after workflow, human/agent task split, supervision ratio hypothesis, autonomy limits supported by evaluation, value baseline, owner and refresh plan.
Prerequisites: One candidate workflow, operational baseline and access to the process owner.

Title: Build, evaluate and secure a scoped agent
Owner: AI engineering + AppSec + domain evaluation lead
Why internal: The capstone must exercise approved architecture, identities, deployment controls and bank-specific test evidence.
Agenda: 2h configure an existing approved scaffold; 2h tests and human-label calibration; 2h attack, recovery and production-monitoring rehearsal; 1h evidence dossier. Reuse one project across the pathway.
Assessment evidence: Versioned implementation and test cases, human-checked judge results, working controls, attack/recovery trace, monitoring and ownership record.
Prerequisites: Prepared scaffold and sandbox; Python readiness. Seven hours assumes adaptation of a scaffold, not a production build from scratch.

Title: Independent technical challenge
Why internal: An independent test establishes the demonstrated scope and residual gaps.
Agenda: 75m reproduce an unseen failure and recovery; 30m design/evidence challenge; 15m feedback and permitted-scope record.
Assessment evidence: Reproducible test evidence and pass on all critical controls within the authorised action class.
Prerequisites: Calibrated challenge pack distinct from practice.

Title: Workflow, supervision and accountability studio
Why internal: N14 concerns real workflow allocation, approval gates, workload and accountability. A workshop with the actual process owner is more actionable than generic organisational-redesign teaching.
Agenda: 30m current workflow; 45m autonomy/approval design; 30m value and oversight measures; 15m ownership agreement.
Assessment evidence: An approved before/after workflow, human/agent task split, supervision ratio hypothesis, autonomy limits supported by evaluation, value baseline, owner and refresh plan.
Prerequisites: Use the same workflow and shared studio template as technical colleagues.

Title: Bank AI-risk and assurance evidence case
Owner: AI risk lead + assurance lead + domain evaluator
Why internal: Risk acceptance, vendor approval and control ownership depend on the internal governance process.
Agenda: 1h inventory and risk scenario; 1h control/vendor dossier; 1h independent-test and judge-evidence review; 1h risk decision and escalation. Map local obligations only for the role and jurisdictions concerned.
Assessment evidence: Traceable risk decision, control evidence, vendor challenge, human-labelled evaluation sample and named residual-risk owner.
Prerequisites: Approved templates, risk appetite, review forum and a redacted vendor/use-case dossier.

Title: Independent governance challenge
Why internal: Assess whether the learner can challenge evidence and defend a decision.
Agenda: 75m evidence challenge; 30m reviewer calibration; 15m feedback and decision-rights record.
Assessment evidence: Defend the risk decision with test evidence, recognise weak automated evaluation and specify unresolved conditions.

Title: Operating-model and tool-selection decision studio
Owner: CIO strategy lead + process owners + AI risk lead
Why internal: N14 concerns real workflow allocation, approval gates, workload and accountability. A workshop with the actual process owner is more actionable than generic organisational-redesign teaching.
Agenda: 30m workflow/value baseline; 45m vendor and autonomy decision; 30m supervision capacity and junior-skill retention; 15m ownership and next evidence request.
Assessment evidence: An approved before/after workflow, human/agent task split, supervision ratio hypothesis, autonomy limits supported by evaluation, value baseline, owner and refresh plan. Challenge at least one vendor claim and one weak evaluation result.
Prerequisites: Common studio template, vendor evidence and budget/role constraints.

Title: Quarterly evidence and adoption forums
Why internal: Leaders need repeated decisions using actual adoption and control evidence.
Agenda: Four 1h forums: baseline and test-set quality; autonomy and judge validation; production drift/value; refresh and accountability. Include a short coached lesson before the decision.
Assessment evidence: Four decision records connecting evaluation results to adoption, supervision capacity, permissions and investment.
Prerequisites: Quarterly portfolio evidence, human-labelled samples and attendance by accountable owners.
